speaker: gm
text:
Mid-morning, behind the King’s Granary: wet cobbles, pigeons, and the smell of grain gone damp. A clerk turns slowly from the sack hoist above the shut loft door, his stockinged feet swinging. A pigeon watches from the beam. Beneath him, a scrawny boy in enormous black boots lobs gutter stones.

“Spin, then! Cob’s got more aim than you had sense!”

From the yard wall, a sharp-faced girl in a shawl swears at everyone in Common, then switches to dock cant for emphasis.

Sergeant Kell steps away from the gate, notebook open. “Sergeant Agnes Kell. The Captain calls it suicide.” Her pencil rests above the page. “I haven’t written that down.” A stone clangs off the hoist hook.

speech.tag: the boy in the too-big boots
speech.speaker: cob

marks.note: This hoist lifts grain sacks into the tally loft; its rope runs through a slot above the loft door and is tied off inside.
In the granary quarter, when Kell has written something down, people take it as true—and too late to change.

speaker: player
text: Nell. Don't write that down either. (I don't look at the body yet. I slip along the wall toward the girl in the shawl, quiet, listening to what she's swearing in cant.)

speaker: gm
text:
“Nell Quickfingers. Noted.” Her pencil scratches once. “The introduction, not the joke.”

You move along the wall, quiet. The girl’s heels drum the bricks as she mutters in a rapid tumble of dock cant; you catch the words for “bluebottle” and “good coat,” delivered with particular contempt. Her eyes flick to Kell’s notebook, then to you.

“You’re not writing that down, are you?” She shifts on the wall, one fist still closed. “Or is this the bit where the nice little investigator pretends they’re not with the bluebottles?”

marks.note: Bluebottle” is dock cant for a watch officer. The girl is using it as an insult, and “good coat” is part of her contemptuous muttering about the watch.
You told Kell not to write down her conclusion, and the girl has just seen Kell write down your introduction. She’s checking whether you’re going to record what she says too.

speaker: player
text: (I answer in cant, low, so Kell can't follow) I'm with nobody, sister. The bluebottle's a loan. What's in the fist? (I nod at her closed hand.)

speaker: dice
text: Persuasion check to get the girl to tell you what’s in her fist: 17 + 0 = 17 vs DC 18: failure

speaker: gm
text:
The girl bares her teeth and shifts farther along the wall, putting another brick between you.

“Good coat, bad ears. Keep your nose out of my hand.”

She watches you more closely, fist still shut. Behind you, a stone clacks against the hoist hook.

marks.note: You asked what she was holding, and she’s keeping it from you; calling you “good coat” also echoes her suspicion that you’re with the watch.

speaker: player
text: Suit yourself. (I leave her be and drift over toward the boy, eyeing those big black boots against the dead man's stockinged feet.) Nice boots, Spin. Bit roomy. Where'd a lad like you come by a pair like that?

speaker: dice
text: Persuasion check to pull it off: 10 + 0 = 10 vs DC 10: success

speaker: gm
text:
Cob’s stone pauses mid-throw. He looks from your face to the dangling feet, then down at his boots.

“Found ’em.”

He stamps one oversized toe against the cobbles. The left boot gives a little crackle. Cob glances at it, then quickly back at you.

“Mister Prout didn’t need ’em. And Cob does.” He squares his shoulders. “They’re Cob’s, so don’t go getting ideas, Quickfingers.”

speaker: player
text: Wouldn't dream of it, Cob. (I crouch like I'm admiring the stitching, tap the left boot with a knuckle to keep his eyes on my face, and slide two fingers down inside the cuff for whatever's crackling in there.)

speaker: dice
text: Deception check to slip your fingers into Cob’s boot and take whatever is crackling inside: 11 + 2 = 13 vs DC 18: failure

speaker: gm
text:
Cob catches your fingers at the boot’s cuff and jerks away, clutching it to his chest.

“Oi! Keep your grubby mitts off!”

The girl drops from the wall between you. Cob backs toward the water butt, eyes fixed on you over the boot.

“Touch him again and see what happens.”

Across the yard, Kell turns at the commotion, notebook still open.

marks.note: You slipped your fingers into Cob’s boot, and he caught you at it.
You tried to take whatever was crackling in Cob’s boot, and she’s warning you off him.
